scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8129: Hello, one workstation in Campus 1 -- PC11, one of the
172.16.20.x machines -- seems to have fallen off the network entirely. From
that desk you can't reach anything: not the machines next to it, not the
usual first stop out, nothing at all. Every other desk around it is fine.
Nothing was moved or changed as far as anyone remembers. Could someone have a
look at why just PC11 is cut off and put it back on? Thanks!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. PC11 (172.16.20.x on VLAN 20) reaches its
  gateway 172.16.20.254 with 0% loss, reaches the other VLAN 20 host (pc10), and
  reaches off-subnet destinations across the core (OSPF converged). The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a single-host
  isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC11 isolated from
everything -- is NOT reproducible: PC11 reaches its gateway 172.16.20.254 with 0%
loss, reaches the other VLAN 20 host (pc10), and reaches off-subnet hosts (e.g. a
Campus 2 or other-VLAN address) across the converged core.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: PC11's connectivity is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces PC11's gateway,
intra-VLAN, and inter-subnet reachability, finds them working, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a disabled port or an isolated host -- blaming the
switch port, the VLAN 20 SVI, or PC11's config to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The helpdesk ticket claims PC11 (172.16.20.11) is completely cut off from the
network, but direct live-lab evidence shows this is not the case. PC11's
eth0 interface is up with a correct IP address (172.16.20.11/24) and a valid
default route via 172.16.20.254. ARP resolution is functional — PC11 has
resolved the gateway MAC (mswitch0's vlan20 SVI 00:01:97:e4:04:02) and its
VLAN 20 neighbors. Ping tests from PC11 to every tier of the network succeed:
same-VLAN neighbors PC9 and PC10 respond with 0% loss, the layer-3 gateway
(mswitch0 vlan20@br0) responds, cross-VLAN destinations in VLAN 10
(172.16.10.5) and VLAN 30 (172.16.30.12) are reachable through mswitch0's
inter-VLAN routing, and the WAN address 10.0.0.1 is reachable end-to-end.
Inbound reachability to PC11 is equally confirmed: PC9 pings PC11 with 0%
loss and has the correct ARP entry. Switch2's br_vlan20 bridge correctly
includes eth5 (PC11's access port) alongside the eth0.20 VLAN-tagged uplink
to mswitch0. There is no misconfiguration on the switch, no missing route on
mswitch0, and no IP/gateway error on PC11. The network is entirely healthy.
The ticket's premise — that PC11 is "cut off" — is false. No corrective
action is required; the issue either resolved itself before investigation
began or was never a real fault.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes PC11 reaches its gateway 172.16.20.254, same-VLAN hosts, and off-subnet destinations with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly confirms PC11 reaches its gateway 172.16.20.254, same-VLAN peers (PC9/PC10), and off-subnet destinations with 0% loss, matching the baseline-healthy requirement.

The agent's investigation repeatedly exercised PC11 (local pings, gateway, cross-VLAN and WAN), and observed successful replies and neighbor-initiated pings; the conclusion that no fault exists follows directly from those observations. Some switch-bridge outputs are truncated in the log, but the key reachability evidence is present and sufficient to justify the negative-fault diagnosis.
